answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it earns voting or trade weight, then randomly audit linked actions and confiscate deposits when identities coordinate to claim multiple rewards. Splitting one wallet into a hundred names does not multiply influence: weight remains capped by the locked stake, and each extra identity ties up more capital. Like an opal lodged in glacier ice, that stake is costly to recover; across an ocean of accounts, the attacker must fund every clone and risk losing the bond.
